continuum theory for CFS simulation of gas solid flow is still in its infancy, and more efforts are needed in order to improve the accuracy of continuum modeling of gas-solid flow and to extend the scope of continuum modeling to more complex situations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the continuum modeling of gas fluidization is not just a simple matter of using a proper constitutive relationships, but it is a multiscale problem, which needs a proper treatment of the effects of meso and sub grid scale structures.

the mesoscale structures play a critical role in the hydrodynamics and transport processes of gas solid fluidizations, and their explicit and/or implicit resolution is the key for the success of the CFD simulation of complex gas solid flows.

, the continuum theory is still a very useful and powerful method for simulating gas solid fluidization and other complex particulate flows, and it can be further improved by incorporating mesoscale structures and sub grid scale models into the constitutive relationships, especially the interphase drag and particle phase stress models.
